texts: bad: "on the thirtieth night of the solo stretch" has no encodable form, and the translator ranked the wrong thing — the parse says the *lighting* was thirtieth and puts the stretch itself in the rank's scale slot, so it asserts something the sentence never says while the night it does rank gets no time link at all. Take the rank out of the adjunct chain and state it as a count in its own finite clause: "On day 259 of Year 1, Coraline Ash lit the lantern of the Harbor Station at sundown. That night she completed thirty solo nights." (the next sentence then restates the count, so you may drop it).
good. the thirty solo nights come out as one counted set of nights that she completed, with the compound correctly unpacked to the night kind.

mixed: the possession, the count and "reached thirty" all come out right, but the compound "solo count" is unpacked into an extra atom saying the count itself is solo — false, and nothing the sentence claims. Reword so "solo" modifies the nights rather than the count: "Coraline Ash's count of solo nights reached thirty."

good. the past copular wraps the property and reuses the count introduced by the previous sentence; if you reword that one, keep the same noun phrase here so both sentences still point at a single count.
good. "met" is treated as one joint event with both people as participants (not two separate meetings), and dawn plus the Year-1 / day-260 date sit on it.
good. "walked back" is kept whole as one verb, both walkers are participants in the single event that "together" calls for, and Aelmere is its destination.

good. the Council stays one participant (no invented name, and nothing is claimed about individual councillors), "in an informal session" keeps its surface preposition, and the date rides the meeting.
good. the investiture comes out as a past event with the Council acting on Coraline Ash, plus the resulting keeper state and a flat "she is a Keeper" fact so a later question resolves.

bad: "her first lantern as a Keeper" loses its restriction — the parse records rank 1 over every lighting she has ever done, which flatly contradicts the day-259 lighting earlier in this same passage; "her first lantern" also mints a second, separate lantern with no link back to the Harbor Station one. A rank taken within a role or phase has no carrier, so state the sequence instead: "After the Council invested her, Coraline Ash lit the lantern of the Harbor Station at sundown. She had not lit a lantern as a Keeper before that." (keep "her own lantern" in place of "the lantern of the Harbor Station" if a different lantern is meant).
good. the hand is what gets moved, the shoulder is attached to Coraline Ash as a body part, and no relation between Meren and the hand is invented.

good. the repeating comes out as a past event with Meren as the speaker and the phrase as its object; "the phrase" has no earlier mention in the passage, so it stands as an unspecified phrase — correct for the text, but the parse never records what was said.

good. "every villager present" becomes a fireable rule — being present rides as a condition rather than being asserted of villagers at large, each villager gets their own repeat event, the phrase is the same one from the previous sentence, and the quantifier word itself is recorded.
